HEXACO responses of real people, for checking synthetic respondents

Source: R/data.R
hexaco_real.Rd

Answers of 17,874 adults from Canada, Great Britain and the United States to the 240 items of the IPIP-HEXACO, a public-domain measure of the six HEXACO personality traits (Ashton, Lee & Goldberg, 2007). The respondents were volunteers who took the inventory online through the Open-Source Psychometrics Project, which posted the data in 2014. They are the real comparison sample for the language model responses in hexaco_llm.

Usage

hexaco_real

Format

A data frame with 17,874 rows (one per respondent) and 241 columns: country (factor: Canada (1,708), Great Britain (1,149) or United States (15,017)) and the 240 items, named as in hexaco_items$item (for example HSinc1, the first Sincerity item).

Source

Open-Source Psychometrics Project, http://openpsychometrics.org/_rawdata/ (HEXACO data, 2014; 22,786 respondents from all countries). The script is data-raw/hexaco.R in the package's GitHub repository.

Details

Answers are on a 7-point scale (1 = strongly disagree, 2 = disagree, 3 = slightly disagree, 4 = neutral, 5 = slightly agree, 6 = agree, 7 = strongly agree) and are stored as given: Reverse-keyed items are not reversed. Use hexaco_items$reverse and 8 - x before scoring. The 117 answers outside 1 to 7 in the original file (coded 0) are NA.

References

Ashton, M. C., Lee, K., & Goldberg, L. R. (2007). The IPIP-HEXACO scales: An alternative, public-domain measure of the personality constructs in the HEXACO model. Personality and Individual Differences, 42(8), 1515-1526. doi:10.1016/j.paid.2006.10.027

See also

hexaco_llm for the language model answers to the same items, hexaco_items for the items and their keys, synthetic_coverage() and authenticity_benchmark().

Examples

table(hexaco_real$country)
#> 
#>        Canada Great Britain United States 
#>          1708          1149         15017 
# Honesty-Humility scores, with reverse-keyed items reversed
h <- hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$trait == "H"]
x <- hexaco_real[h]
rev <- intersect(h, hexaco_items$item[hexaco_items$reverse])
x[rev] <- 8 - x[rev]
tapply(rowMeans(x, na.rm = TRUE), hexaco_real$country, mean)
#>        Canada Great Britain United States 
#>      4.456342      4.357440      4.443543
